Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	package server

3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"io"
7		"mime"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"

11		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/app"
12		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
13	)
14	
15	// maxChunkBytes caps a single inbound chunk body.
16	const maxChunkBytes = 64 << 20
17	
18	type attachmentRequest struct {
19		ID         string          `json:"attachmentId"`
20		TotalBytes json.RawMessage `json:"totalBytes"`
21		ChunkSize  json.RawMessage `json:"chunkSize"`
22		SHA256     string          `json:"sha256"`
23	}
24	
25	// attachmentListEntry is one item of the attachment listing response.
26	type attachmentListEntry struct {
27		ID             string  `json:"attachmentId"`
28		TotalBytes     int64   `json:"totalBytes"`
29		ChunkSize      int64   `json:"chunkSize"`
30		SHA256         string  `json:"sha256"`
31		Complete       bool    `json:"complete"`
32		Owned          bool    `json:"owned"`
33		ReceivedChunks []int64 `json:"receivedChunks"`
34	}
35	
36	// handleListAttachments is the read-only listing over the attachment
37	// collection: every upload the device in the path created plus every upload
38	// another device created and granted it read access to, each at most once,
39	// ordered by creation ascending. limit (1..1000, default 100) and offset
40	// (non-negative, default 0) page the result; an illegal value is a 400 JSON
41	// error checked before the device lookup. An unregistered device is a 404
42	// JSON error with no listing. The handler writes nothing: no attachment,
43	// chunk or access state changes.
44	func handleListAttachments(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
45		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
46	
47		limit, offset, ok := parseAttachmentListQuery(w, r)
48		if !ok {
49			return
50		}
51	
52		items, err := s.ListAttachments(deviceID, limit, offset)
53		if err != nil {
54			switch {
55			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
56				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
57			default:
58				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to list attachments")
59			}
60			return
61		}
62	
63		entries := make([]attachmentListEntry, 0, len(items))
64		for _, item := range items {
65			entries = append(entries, attachmentListEntry{
66				ID:             item.ID,
67				TotalBytes:     item.TotalBytes,
68				ChunkSize:      item.ChunkSize,
69				SHA256:         item.SHA256,
70				Complete:       item.Complete,
71				Owned:          item.Owned,
72				ReceivedChunks: item.ReceivedChunks,
73			})
74		}
75	
76		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachments": entries})
77	}

79	// parseAttachmentListQuery parses the limit/offset pagination parameters of
80	// the attachment listing, writing the documented 400 on an illegal value.
81	func parseAttachmentListQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (limit, offset int64, ok bool) {
82		q := r.URL.Query()
83	
84		limit = defaultListLimit
85		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
86			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
87			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
88				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
89				return 0, 0, false
90			}
91			limit = v
92		}
93	
94		offset = 0
95		if raw := q.Get("offset"); raw != "" {
96			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
97			if err != nil || v < 0 {
98				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "offset must be a non-negative integer")
99				return 0, 0, false
100			}
101			offset = v
102		}
103	
104		return limit, offset, true
105	}

107	// handleCreateAttachment registers a resumable chunked upload for the device
108	// in the path. The body is strict JSON carrying the stable attachment id, the
109	// declared total size and chunk size (positive integers) and the lowercase
110	// hex SHA-256 of the final content. Any malformed input is a 400 JSON error
111	// and writes nothing; an unregistered device is a 404; an id already taken —
112	// by another device, or by this device with different metadata — is a 409
113	// that leaves the original record untouched.
114	func handleCreateAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
115		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
116	
117		var req attachmentRequest
118		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
119			return
120		}
121		if req.ID == "" {
122			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "attachmentId must be a non-empty string")
123			return
124		}
125		totalBytes, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.TotalBytes)
126		if !ok {
127			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "totalBytes must be a positive integer")
128			return
129		}
130		chunkSize, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.ChunkSize)
131		if !ok {
132			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunkSize must be a positive integer")
133			return
134		}
135		if !isLowerHexSHA256(req.SHA256) {
136			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "sha256 must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
137			return
138		}
139	
140		created, err := s.CreateAttachment(deviceID, store.Attachment{
141			ID:         req.ID,
142			TotalBytes: totalBytes,
143			ChunkSize:  chunkSize,
144			SHA256:     req.SHA256,
145		})
146		if err != nil {
147			var conflict *store.ErrAttachmentConflict
148			switch {
149			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
150				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
151			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
152				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "attachmentId already exists with a different owner or metadata: "+conflict.ID)
153			default:
154				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to create attachment")
155			}
156			return
157		}
158	
159		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": req.ID, "created": created})
160	}
161	
162	// handlePutChunk stores one binary chunk of an upload. The request must be
163	// application/octet-stream; the index is zero-based and chunks may arrive in
164	// any order. An unknown attachment is a 404 and a non-creator device a 403; a
165	// wrong content type, an out-of-range index, a short non-final chunk or a
166	// final chunk beyond the declared total is a 400 — none of these write
167	// anything. Re-submitting identical bytes is idempotent; different bytes for
168	// the same index are a 409 and the first content is kept. Once the upload is
169	// finished it is sealed: every further chunk write, even a byte-identical
170	// one, is a 409 and the stored content is unchanged.
171	func handlePutChunk(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
172		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
173		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
174	
175		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
176		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/octet-stream" {
177			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/octet-stream")
178			return
179		}
180	
181		index, ok := parseCursorPath(r.PathValue("index"))
182		if !ok {
183			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunk index must be a non-negative integer")
184			return
185		}
186	
187		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxChunkBytes+1)
188		data, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
189		if err != nil || int64(len(data)) > maxChunkBytes {
190			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunk body is too large")
191			return
192		}
193	
194		created, err := s.PutChunk(deviceID, attachmentID, index, data)
195		if err != nil {
196			var invalid *store.ErrChunkInvalid
197			var conflict *store.ErrChunkConflict
198			switch {
199			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
200				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
201			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
202				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
203			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentSealed):
204				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "attachment is complete and no longer accepts chunks")
205			case errors.As(err, &invalid):
206				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, invalid.Reason)
207			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
208				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "chunk already exists with different content")
209			default:
210				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to store chunk")
211			}
212			return
213		}
214	
215		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"index": index, "created": created})
216	}
217	
218	// handleCompleteAttachment seals an upload. Only the creating device may
219	// finish it (others get a 403; an unknown attachment a 404). Missing chunks
220	// or a total-length mismatch are a 409 and leave the upload resumable; a
221	// digest mismatch is a 422 and leaves it incomplete. When another finished
222	// attachment already holds the same digest and size, the content is reused
223	// without copying bytes (reused=true); the same digest at a different size is
224	// a 409. A successful or repeated finish returns the same recorded result.
225	func handleCompleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
226		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
227		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
228	
229		result, err := s.CompleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID)
230		if err != nil {
231			switch {
232			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
233				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
234			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
235				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
236			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentIncomplete):
237				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "chunks are missing or do not add up to the declared total")
238			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch):
239				writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "assembled content does not match the declared sha256")
240			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentDigestConflict):
241				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "a completed content with the same digest but a different size exists")
242			default:
243				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to complete attachment")
244			}

246		}

248		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
249	}

251	// handleGetAttachment returns the reader's view of an upload: the original
252	// metadata, the sorted indices received so far and the completion status. The
253	// creator and any device granted access through the access endpoint see the
254	// same body; any other device gets a 403, an unknown attachment a 404.
255	func handleGetAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
256		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
257		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
258	
259		a, indices, err := s.GetAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID)
260		if err != nil {
261			switch {
262			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
263				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
264			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
265				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
266			default:
267				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to load attachment")
268			}
269			return
270		}
271	
272		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
273			"attachmentId":   a.ID,
274			"totalBytes":     a.TotalBytes,
275			"chunkSize":      a.ChunkSize,
276			"sha256":         a.SHA256,
277			"complete":       a.Complete,
278			"receivedChunks": indices,
279		})

282	// handleGetChunk streams one stored chunk back to the creator or a granted
283	// reader. An empty identifier is rejected by the path guard; an illegal index
284	// is a 400; an unknown attachment or a chunk that never arrived is a 404; any
285	// other device is a 403.
286	func handleGetChunk(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
287		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
288		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

290		index, ok := parseCursorPath(r.PathValue("index"))
291		if !ok {

297		if err != nil {
298			var invalid *store.ErrChunkInvalid

300			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
301				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
302			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrChunkNotFound):
303				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "chunk not found")
304			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):

314		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")

319	// handleListAttachmentAccess is the read-only roster over an attachment's
320	// access subresource: the device ids the attachment is currently open to for
321	// reading — every device the creator granted through the access endpoint and
322	// that has not been revoked — each at most once, ordered by the time their
323	// latest grant took effect ascending. The creator itself is not part of the
324	// roster (its reads come from ownership, so a self grant/revoke neither adds
325	// nor removes an entry). Only the attachment's creator may read it — the
326	// device in the path is the caller identity and there is no other
327	// authentication: an unknown or deleted attachment is a 404 and a non-creator
328	// caller a 403, judged independently. Pagination shares the attachment
329	// listing's limit/offset parsing, so an illegal value is a 400 checked before
330	// the attachment lookup. The handler writes nothing: no access row, chunk or
331	// attachment state changes.
332	func handleListAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
333		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
334		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
335	
336		limit, offset, ok := parseAttachmentListQuery(w, r)
337		if !ok {
338			return
339		}
340	
341		devices, err := s.ListAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, limit, offset)
342		if err != nil {
343			switch {
344			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
345				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
346			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
347				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
348			default:
349				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to list attachment access")
350			}
351			return
352		}
353	
354		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"devices": devices})
355	}

357	// handleSetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes a registered device's read
358	// access to one attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
359	// unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write; repeating the current
360	// state is idempotent (changed=false). Only the creator may change access: a
361	// non-creator caller gets a 403 and an unknown attachment a 404, neither
362	// touching any access state. A rejected request (bad content type, malformed
363	// JSON, trailing content, empty or mistyped fields, unknown action) is a 400
364	// JSON error and writes nothing; an unregistered target device is a 404 JSON
365	// error. A granted device reads the same metadata and chunk bytes as the
366	// creator; a revoke returns its reads to 403 at once and never deletes
367	// stored chunks or sealed content.
368	func handleSetAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
369		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
370		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
371	
372		var req permissionRequest
373		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
374			return
375		}
376		if req.DeviceID == "" {
377			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
378			return
379		}
380		var authorized bool
381		switch req.Action {
382		case "grant":
383			authorized = true
384		case "revoke":
385			authorized = false
386		default:
387			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `action must be "grant" or "revoke"`)
388			return
389		}
390	
391		changed, err := s.SetAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, req.DeviceID, authorized)
392		if err != nil {
393			switch {
394			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
395				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
396			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
397				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
398			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
399				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
400			default:
401				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to update attachment access")
402			}
403			return
404		}
405	
406		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
407			"deviceId":   req.DeviceID,
408			"authorized": authorized,
409			"changed":    changed,
410		})
411	}
412	
413	// handleDeleteAttachment removes an upload outright. Only the creating device
414	// may delete: any other device gets a 403 and an unknown (or already deleted)
415	// id a 404, neither writing anything. A successful delete answers the
416	// attachment id and a deletion marker, after which the record, its chunks,
417	// its completion state and every access grant are gone: every later read,
418	// chunk write, finish or access change against the id is a 404, and
419	// re-creating the id starts a brand-new upload. Digest-addressed content is
420	// reclaimed only when no finished attachment references it any longer.
421	func handleDeleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
422		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
423		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
424	
425		if err := s.DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID); err != nil {
426			switch {
427			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
428				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
429			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
430				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
431			default:
432				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to delete attachment")
433			}
434			return
435		}
436	
437		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": attachmentID, "deleted": true})
438	}

440	// isLowerHexSHA256 reports whether s is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
441	func isLowerHexSHA256(s string) bool {
442		if len(s) != 64 {
443			return false
444		}
445		for _, c := range s {
446			if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
447				return false
448			}
449		}
450		return true
451	}

11	// ErrAttachmentNotFound reports that no attachment exists with the given id.
12	// The caller maps it to 404.
13	var ErrAttachmentNotFound = errors.New("attachment not found")
14	
15	// ErrAttachmentForbidden reports that the device in the path is not the
16	// device that created the attachment. The caller maps it to 403.
17	var ErrAttachmentForbidden = errors.New("attachment belongs to another device")
18	
19	// ErrAttachmentIncomplete reports that a finish was attempted before every
20	// chunk arrived, or the received bytes do not add up to the declared total.
21	// The upload stays resumable; the caller maps it to 409.
22	var ErrAttachmentIncomplete = errors.New("attachment chunks are missing or shorter than the declared total")
23	
24	// ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch reports that the assembled content does not
25	// hash to the declared digest. The attachment stays incomplete; the caller
26	// maps it to 422.
27	var ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch = errors.New("assembled content does not match the declared sha256")

29	// ErrAttachmentDigestConflict reports that a different-size completed content
30	// already exists under the same digest, so this upload cannot be finished or
31	// reused. The upload stays resumable; the caller maps it to 409.

34	// ErrAttachmentConflict reports that an attachment id is already taken — by
35	// another device, or by this device with different metadata. The original
36	// record is unchanged; the caller maps it to 409.
37	type ErrAttachmentConflict struct {
38		ID string
39	}
40	
41	func (e *ErrAttachmentConflict) Error() string {
42		return fmt.Sprintf("attachment %q already exists with different owner or metadata", e.ID)
43	}

45	// ErrAttachmentSealed reports a chunk write to an upload that was already
46	// finished. A sealed attachment is immutable: every further chunk write —
47	// even a byte-identical resubmission — is rejected and the recorded state and
48	// content are left unchanged. The caller maps it to 409.
49	var ErrAttachmentSealed = errors.New("attachment is complete and no longer accepts chunks")

51	// ErrChunkInvalid reports a chunk that violates the upload's declared shape:
52	// an out-of-range index, a non-final chunk shorter than the declared chunk
53	// size, or a final chunk beyond the declared total. The caller maps it to
54	// 400; nothing is written.
55	type ErrChunkInvalid struct {
56		Reason string
57	}
58	
59	func (e *ErrChunkInvalid) Error() string { return e.Reason }
60	
61	// ErrChunkConflict reports that a chunk index already holds different bytes.
62	// The first content is kept; the caller maps it to 409.
63	type ErrChunkConflict struct {
64		Index int64
65	}
66	
67	func (e *ErrChunkConflict) Error() string {
68		return fmt.Sprintf("chunk %d already exists with different content", e.Index)
69	}

72	// caller maps it to 404.

75	// Attachment is the stored metadata of one resumable upload.
76	type Attachment struct {
77		ID         string
78		DeviceID   string
79		TotalBytes int64
80		ChunkSize  int64
81		SHA256     string
82		Complete   bool
83		Reused     bool
84	}

86	// CompleteResult reports the outcome of a successful (or repeated) finish.
87	type CompleteResult struct {
88		ID       string `json:"attachmentId"`
89		Size     int64  `json:"size"`
90		SHA256   string `json:"sha256"`
91		Complete bool   `json:"complete"`
92		Reused   bool   `json:"reused"`
93	}

95	// chunkCount returns how many chunks the declared shape implies.
96	func (a Attachment) chunkCount() int64 {
97		return (a.TotalBytes + a.ChunkSize - 1) / a.ChunkSize
98	}
99	
100	// checkChunkShape validates index and len(data) against the declared
101	// totalBytes/chunkSize, returning *ErrChunkInvalid on any violation.
102	func (a Attachment) checkChunkShape(index int64, length int64) error {
103		count := a.chunkCount()
104		if index < 0 || index >= count {
105			return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("chunk index %d is out of range [0, %d)", index, count)}
106		}
107		if index < count-1 {
108			if length != a.ChunkSize {
109				return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("non-final chunk %d must be exactly %d bytes", index, a.ChunkSize)}
110			}
111			return nil
112		}
113		remaining := a.TotalBytes - a.ChunkSize*(count-1)
114		if length < 1 || length > remaining {
115			return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("final chunk must be between 1 and %d bytes", remaining)}
116		}
117		return nil
118	}

120	// loadAttachmentTx loads an attachment row inside tx without any ownership
121	// judgment; an unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound.
122	func loadAttachmentTx(tx *sql.Tx, id string) (Attachment, error) {
123		var a Attachment
124		var complete, reused int
125		err := tx.QueryRow(
126			`SELECT id, device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256, complete, reused
127			 FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, id,
128		).Scan(&a.ID, &a.DeviceID, &a.TotalBytes, &a.ChunkSize, &a.SHA256, &complete, &reused)
129		switch {
130		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
131			return Attachment{}, ErrAttachmentNotFound
132		case err != nil:
133			return Attachment{}, err
134		}
135		a.Complete = complete != 0
136		a.Reused = reused != 0
137		return a, nil
138	}

140	// getAttachmentTx loads an attachment row inside tx and enforces ownership:
141	// an unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a device other than the
142	// creator yields ErrAttachmentForbidden.
143	func getAttachmentTx(tx *sql.Tx, id, deviceID string) (Attachment, error) {
144		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, id)
145		if err != nil {
146			return Attachment{}, err
147		}
148		if a.DeviceID != deviceID {
149			return Attachment{}, ErrAttachmentForbidden
150		}
151		return a, nil
152	}

154	// getAttachmentReadTx loads an attachment row inside tx and enforces read
155	// access: the creator, or a device the creator has granted access through
156	// SetAttachmentAccess, may read; any other device yields
157	// ErrAttachmentForbidden. An unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound.
158	func getAttachmentReadTx(tx *sql.Tx, id, deviceID string) (Attachment, error) {
159		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, id)
160		if err != nil {
161			return Attachment{}, err
162		}
163		if a.DeviceID == deviceID {
164			return a, nil
165		}
166		granted, err := attachmentAccessGrantedTx(tx, id, deviceID)
167		if err != nil {
168			return Attachment{}, err
169		}
170		if !granted {

176	// attachmentAccessGrantedTx reports whether deviceID currently holds read
177	// access to the attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
178	// unauthorized, so an absent row means not granted.
179	func attachmentAccessGrantedTx(tx *sql.Tx, attachmentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
180		var stored int
181		err := tx.QueryRow(
182			`SELECT authorized FROM attachment_access WHERE attachment_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
183			attachmentID, deviceID,
184		).Scan(&stored)
185		switch {
186		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
187			return false, nil
188		case err != nil:
189			return false, err
190		default:
191			return stored != 0, nil
192		}

195	// CreateAttachment registers a new resumable upload owned by deviceID.
196	//
197	//   - An unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
198	//   - Re-posting identical metadata under the same device is idempotent
199	//     (created=false).
200	//   - An id already taken — by another device (even with identical metadata)
201	//     or by this device with different metadata — yields
202	//     *ErrAttachmentConflict; the original record is unchanged.
203	//
204	// The check and the insert run in one serialized transaction and commit
205	// synchronously, so a retry after a crash reaches the same decision.
206	func (s *Store) CreateAttachment(deviceID string, a Attachment) (created bool, err error) {
207		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
208		if err != nil {
209			return false, err
210		}
211		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
212	
213		var deviceExists bool
214		if err := tx.QueryRow(
215			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
216		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
217			return false, err
218		}
219		if !deviceExists {
220			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
221		}
222	
223		var owner string
224		var totalBytes, chunkSize int64
225		var digest string
226		err = tx.QueryRow(
227			`SELECT device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256 FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, a.ID,
228		).Scan(&owner, &totalBytes, &chunkSize, &digest)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
231			// The creation sequence is one past the current maximum, assigned
232			// inside the same serialized transaction as the insert, so values are
233			// unique, monotone and never reused — a deleted id that is created
234			// again lists as a brand-new record at the end.
235			if _, err := tx.Exec(
236				`INSERT INTO attachments (id, device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256, complete, reused, created_seq)
237				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(created_seq), 0) + 1 FROM attachments))`,
238				a.ID, deviceID, a.TotalBytes, a.ChunkSize, a.SHA256,
239			); err != nil {
240				return false, err
241			}
242			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
243				return false, err
244			}
245			return true, nil
246		case err != nil:
247			return false, err
248		}
249	
250		if owner != deviceID || totalBytes != a.TotalBytes || chunkSize != a.ChunkSize || digest != a.SHA256 {
251			return false, &ErrAttachmentConflict{ID: a.ID}
252		}
253		return false, tx.Commit()
254	}

256	// PutChunk stores one chunk of an upload, durably, inside one transaction.
257	//
258	// Ownership and shape are enforced first: an unknown attachment yields
259	// ErrAttachmentNotFound, a non-creator device ErrAttachmentForbidden, and an
260	// out-of-range index or wrong length *ErrChunkInvalid — none of these write
261	// anything. A finished upload is sealed: any further chunk write, even a
262	// byte-identical resubmission, yields ErrAttachmentSealed and changes
263	// nothing. On an open upload, re-submitting identical bytes for an existing
264	// index is idempotent (created=false); different bytes for the same index
265	// yield *ErrChunkConflict and the first content is kept. Chunks may arrive in
266	// any order.
267	func (s *Store) PutChunk(deviceID, attachmentID string, index int64, data []byte) (created bool, err error) {
268		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
269		if err != nil {
270			return false, err
271		}
272		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
273	
274		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
275		if err != nil {
276			return false, err
277		}
278		// A sealed upload is immutable: reject every further write before any
279		// shape check or content comparison, so the recorded state and content
280		// cannot change once the finish committed.
281		if a.Complete {
282			return false, ErrAttachmentSealed
283		}
284		if err := a.checkChunkShape(index, int64(len(data))); err != nil {
285			return false, err
286		}
287	
288		var existing []byte
289		err = tx.QueryRow(
290			`SELECT data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? AND idx = ?`,
291			attachmentID, index,
292		).Scan(&existing)
293		switch {
294		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
295			if _, err := tx.Exec(
296				`INSERT INTO attachment_chunks (attachment_id, idx, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
297				attachmentID, index, data,
298			); err != nil {
299				return false, err
300			}
301			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
302				return false, err
303			}
304			return true, nil
305		case err != nil:
306			return false, err
307		}
308	
309		if !bytesEqual(existing, data) {
310			return false, &ErrChunkConflict{Index: index}
311		}
312		return false, tx.Commit()
313	}
314	
315	// reuseContentTx resolves the digest-addressed content reuse decision inside
316	// tx: it returns reused=true when finished content with the same digest and
317	// size already exists (the bytes are not copied), reused=false when no such
318	// content exists yet (the caller inserts it), and ErrAttachmentDigestConflict
319	// when a finished content carries the same digest but a different size. That
320	// last state cannot arise from honest chunk assembly without a hash collision,
321	// but it must never silently reuse mismatched bytes.
322	func reuseContentTx(tx *sql.Tx, digest string, size int64) (bool, error) {
323		var contentSize int64
324		err := tx.QueryRow(
325			`SELECT size FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
326		).Scan(&contentSize)
327		switch {
328		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
329			return false, nil
330		case err != nil:
331			return false, err
332		case contentSize != size:
333			return false, ErrAttachmentDigestConflict
334		default:
335			return true, nil
336		}
337	}
338	
339	// CompleteAttachment seals an upload: every declared chunk must be present
340	// and their lengths must add up to the declared total, after which the
341	// concatenated content must hash to the declared digest.
342	//
343	//   - Unknown attachment: ErrAttachmentNotFound; non-creator device:
344	//     ErrAttachmentForbidden.
345	//   - Missing chunks or a total-length mismatch: ErrAttachmentIncomplete; the
346	//     upload stays resumable.
347	//   - Digest mismatch: ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch; the upload stays
348	//     incomplete.
349	//   - A completed content with the same digest but a different size:
350	//     ErrAttachmentDigestConflict; the upload stays resumable.
351	//   - A completed content with the same digest and size is reused: the bytes
352	//     are not copied and the result carries Reused=true.
353	//
354	// A successful finish is persisted with its result, so repeating the call
355	// returns the same result without recomputing anything.
356	func (s *Store) CompleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) (CompleteResult, error) {
357		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
358		if err != nil {
359			return CompleteResult{}, err
360		}
361		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
362	
363		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
364		if err != nil {
365			return CompleteResult{}, err
366		}
367		if a.Complete {
368			// A repeat finish returns the recorded result unchanged.
369			return CompleteResult{
370				ID:       a.ID,
371				Size:     a.TotalBytes,
372				SHA256:   a.SHA256,
373				Complete: true,
374				Reused:   a.Reused,
375			}, tx.Commit()
376		}
377	
378		rows, err := tx.Query(
379			`SELECT idx, data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
380			attachmentID,
381		)
382		if err != nil {
383			return CompleteResult{}, err
384		}
385		var content []byte
386		var received int64
387		var total int64
388		var prevIndex int64 = -1
389		complete := true
390		for rows.Next() {
391			var idx int64
392			var data []byte
393			if err := rows.Scan(&idx, &data); err != nil {
394				_ = rows.Close()
395				return CompleteResult{}, err
396			}
397			if idx != prevIndex+1 {
398				complete = false
399			}
400			prevIndex = idx
401			received++
402			total += int64(len(data))
403			content = append(content, data...)
404		}
405		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
406			_ = rows.Close()
407			return CompleteResult{}, err
408		}
409		_ = rows.Close()
410	
411		if !complete || received != a.chunkCount() || total != a.TotalBytes {
412			return CompleteResult{}, ErrAttachmentIncomplete
413		}
414	
415		sum := sha256.Sum256(content)
416		if hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) != a.SHA256 {
417			return CompleteResult{}, ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch
418		}
419	
420		// Content is addressed by digest: an existing row means another finished
421		// attachment already stored these bytes.
422		reused, err := reuseContentTx(tx, a.SHA256, a.TotalBytes)
423		if err != nil {
424			return CompleteResult{}, err
425		}
426		if !reused {
427			if _, err := tx.Exec(
428				`INSERT INTO attachment_contents (sha256, size, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
429				a.SHA256, a.TotalBytes, content,
430			); err != nil {
431				return CompleteResult{}, err
432			}
433		}
434	
435		if _, err := tx.Exec(
436			`UPDATE attachments SET complete = 1, reused = ? WHERE id = ?`,
437			boolToInt(reused), attachmentID,
438		); err != nil {
439			return CompleteResult{}, err
440		}
441		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
442			return CompleteResult{}, err
443		}
444		return CompleteResult{
445			ID:       a.ID,
446			Size:     a.TotalBytes,
447			SHA256:   a.SHA256,
448			Complete: true,
449			Reused:   reused,
450		}, nil
451	}
452	
453	// GetAttachment returns the stored metadata of an upload together with the
454	// sorted indices of the chunks received so far. An unknown id yields
455	// ErrAttachmentNotFound; a device that is neither the creator nor a granted
456	// reader yields ErrAttachmentForbidden.
457	func (s *Store) GetAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) (Attachment, []int64, error) {
458		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
459		if err != nil {
460			return Attachment{}, nil, err
461		}
462		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
463	
464		a, err := getAttachmentReadTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
465		if err != nil {
466			return Attachment{}, nil, err
467		}
468	
469		rows, err := tx.Query(
470			`SELECT idx FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
471			attachmentID,
472		)
473		if err != nil {
474			return Attachment{}, nil, err
475		}
476		indices := make([]int64, 0)
477		for rows.Next() {
478			var idx int64
479			if err := rows.Scan(&idx); err != nil {
480				_ = rows.Close()
481				return Attachment{}, nil, err
482			}
483			indices = append(indices, idx)
484		}
485		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
486			_ = rows.Close()
487			return Attachment{}, nil, err
488		}
489		_ = rows.Close()
490	
491		return a, indices, tx.Commit()
492	}
493	
494	// GetAttachmentChunk returns the bytes stored at index. An unknown attachment
495	// yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a device that is neither the creator nor a
496	// granted reader yields ErrAttachmentForbidden.
497	// For a known attachment, a negative index or one beyond the declared chunk
498	// range yields *ErrChunkInvalid (the caller maps it to 400); an in-range index
499	// with no stored chunk yields ErrChunkNotFound (404).
500	func (s *Store) GetAttachmentChunk(deviceID, attachmentID string, index int64) ([]byte, error) {
501		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
502		if err != nil {
503			return nil, err
504		}
505		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
506	
507		a, err := getAttachmentReadTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
508		if err != nil {
509			return nil, err
510		}
511		// The path index is already a non-negative decimal; reject one outside the
512		// shape the creator declared so out-of-range reads fail as a 400 rather than
513		// masquerading as a missing chunk (404).
514		if index < 0 || index >= a.chunkCount() {
515			return nil, &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("chunk index %d is out of range [0, %d)", index, a.chunkCount())}
516		}
517	
518		var data []byte
519		err = tx.QueryRow(
520			`SELECT data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? AND idx = ?`,
521			attachmentID, index,
522		).Scan(&data)
523		switch {
524		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
525			return nil, ErrChunkNotFound
526		case err != nil:
527			return nil, err
528		}
529		return data, tx.Commit()
530	}
531	
532	// DeleteAttachment removes the attachment owned by deviceID together with
533	// every trace it left behind: the received chunks, the completion state and
534	// every access grant. An unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a device
535	// other than the creator yields ErrAttachmentForbidden — neither writes
536	// anything, so a repeat delete misses the same way a never-created id does.
537	//
538	// Finished content is addressed by digest and shared across attachments, so
539	// the stored bytes are reclaimed only when the deleted attachment was the
540	// last completed one referencing them; other finished attachments with the
541	// same digest keep reading their content unchanged. An incomplete upload
542	// references no shared content, so deleting it only drops its chunks.
543	//
544	// The check, the row removals and the content reclamation run in one
545	// serialized transaction that commits synchronously, so concurrent deletes of
546	// the same attachment commit at most once and a restart still finds the
547	// attachment gone.
548	func (s *Store) DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) error {
549		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
550		if err != nil {
551			return err
552		}
553		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
554	
555		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
556		if err != nil {
557			return err
558		}
559	
560		if _, err := tx.Exec(
561			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE attachment_id = ?`, attachmentID,
562		); err != nil {
563			return err
564		}
565		if _, err := tx.Exec(
566			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ?`, attachmentID,
567		); err != nil {
568			return err
569		}
570		if _, err := tx.Exec(
571			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, attachmentID,
572		); err != nil {
573			return err
574		}
575	
576		// Reclaim the digest-addressed content only when no completed attachment
577		// references it any longer.
578		if a.Complete {
579			var stillReferenced bool
580			if err := tx.QueryRow(
581				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
582				a.SHA256,
583			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
584				return err
585			}
586			if !stillReferenced {
587				if _, err := tx.Exec(
588					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, a.SHA256,
589				); err != nil {
590					return err
591				}
592			}
593		}
594		return tx.Commit()
595	}
596	
597	// SetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes targetDeviceID's read access to the
598	// attachment, on behalf of callerDeviceID. Every (attachment, device) pair
599	// starts unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write for the pair
600	// (changed=true); repeating the state that already holds writes nothing and
601	// reports changed=false. An unknown attachment yields ErrAttachmentNotFound,
602	// a caller other than the creator ErrAttachmentForbidden, and an unregistered
603	// target device ErrDeviceNotFound — none of these write anything. The lookup
604	// and the write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke
605	// calls each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
606	// action. Access only widens the read paths; chunk writes and the finish stay
607	// creator-only, and a revoke never deletes stored chunks or sealed content.
608	func (s *Store) SetAttachmentAccess(callerDeviceID, attachmentID, targetDeviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
609		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
610		if err != nil {
611			return false, err
612		}
613		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
614	
615		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID)
616		if err != nil {
617			return false, err
618		}
619		if a.DeviceID != callerDeviceID {
620			return false, ErrAttachmentForbidden
621		}
622		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(tx, targetDeviceID)
623		if err != nil {
624			return false, err
625		}
626		if !exists {
627			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
628		}
629	
630		current, err := attachmentAccessGrantedTx(tx, attachmentID, targetDeviceID)
631		if err != nil {
632			return false, err
633		}
634		if current == authorized {
635			return false, tx.Commit()
636		}
637	
638		if authorized {
639			// A (re-)grant takes the next position past the attachment's newest
640			// grant, assigned inside the same serialized transaction, so the
641			// access list orders devices by their latest grant and a position is
642			// never reused even after the previous holder was revoked.
643			var nextSeq int64
644			if err := tx.QueryRow(
645				`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(granted_seq), 0) + 1 FROM attachment_access WHERE attachment_id = ?`,
646				attachmentID,
647			).Scan(&nextSeq); err != nil {
648				return false, err
649			}
650			if _, err := tx.Exec(
651				`INSERT INTO attachment_access (attachment_id, device_id, authorized, granted_seq) VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)
652				 ON CONFLICT (attachment_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = 1, granted_seq = excluded.granted_seq`,
653				attachmentID, targetDeviceID, nextSeq,
654			); err != nil {
655				return false, err
656			}
657		} else {
658			// A revoke only clears the verdict; the row and its last grant
659			// position stay on disk, so an unchanged ledger is byte-for-byte
660			// stable and a later re-grant simply takes a new position.
661			if _, err := tx.Exec(
662				`UPDATE attachment_access SET authorized = 0
663				 WHERE attachment_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
664				attachmentID, targetDeviceID,
665			); err != nil {
666				return false, err
667			}
668		}
669		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
670			return false, err
671		}
672		return true, nil
673	}
674	
675	// ListedAttachment is one entry of a device's attachment listing: the stored
676	// metadata, whether the listing device created the attachment, and the sorted
677	// indices of the chunks received so far.
678	type ListedAttachment struct {
679		Attachment
680		Owned          bool
681		ReceivedChunks []int64
682	}
683	
684	// ListAttachments returns the page of attachments visible to deviceID: every
685	// attachment the device created plus every attachment another device created
686	// and granted it read access to, each appearing at most once. Entries are
687	// ordered by creation sequence ascending — a stable order that survives
688	// restarts and never reuses a position, so a deleted id that is created again
689	// lists as a new record at the end — and paginated by limit/offset. An
690	// unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound and no listing. The read runs
691	// in one serialized transaction and writes nothing.
692	func (s *Store) ListAttachments(deviceID string, limit, offset int64) ([]ListedAttachment, error) {
693		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
694		if err != nil {
695			return nil, err
696		}
697		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
698	
699		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
700		if err != nil {
701			return nil, err
702		}
703		if !exists {
704			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
705		}
706	
707		rows, err := tx.Query(
708			`SELECT a.id, a.device_id, a.total_bytes, a.chunk_size, a.sha256, a.complete
709			 FROM attachments a
710			 WHERE a.device_id = ?
711				OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attachment_access ac
712					WHERE ac.attachment_id = a.id AND ac.device_id = ? AND ac.authorized <> 0)
713			 ORDER BY a.created_seq ASC
714			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
715			deviceID, deviceID, limit, offset,
716		)
717		if err != nil {
718			return nil, err
719		}
720		items := make([]ListedAttachment, 0)
721		for rows.Next() {
722			var item ListedAttachment
723			var complete int
724			if err := rows.Scan(
725				&item.ID, &item.DeviceID, &item.TotalBytes, &item.ChunkSize, &item.SHA256, &complete,
726			); err != nil {
727				_ = rows.Close()
728				return nil, err
729			}
730			item.Complete = complete != 0
731			item.ReceivedChunks = make([]int64, 0)
732			items = append(items, item)
733		}
734		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
735			_ = rows.Close()
736			return nil, err
737		}
738		_ = rows.Close()
739	
740		for i := range items {
741			items[i].Owned = items[i].DeviceID == deviceID
742			chunkRows, err := tx.Query(
743				`SELECT idx FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
744				items[i].ID,
745			)
746			if err != nil {
747				return nil, err
748			}
749			for chunkRows.Next() {
750				var idx int64
751				if err := chunkRows.Scan(&idx); err != nil {
752					_ = chunkRows.Close()
753					return nil, err
754				}
755				items[i].ReceivedChunks = append(items[i].ReceivedChunks, idx)
756			}
757			if err := chunkRows.Err(); err != nil {
758				_ = chunkRows.Close()
759				return nil, err
760			}
761			_ = chunkRows.Close()
762		}
763	
764		return items, tx.Commit()
765	}
766	
767	// ListAttachmentAccess returns the page of device ids that currently hold
768	// granted read access to the attachment, each at most once, ordered by the
769	// time their latest grant took effect ascending: the grant sequence is
770	// assigned one past the attachment's maximum inside the granting
771	// transaction, so a device revoked and re-granted moves to the position of
772	// the new grant and never appears twice. The creator itself is never in the
773	// roster: its reads come from ownership, so a grant or revoke aimed at the
774	// creator's own id neither adds nor removes an entry. Only the creator may
775	// read the list: an unknown attachment yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a
776	// device other than the creator ErrAttachmentForbidden, judged
777	// independently, and neither writes anything. Pagination matches
778	// ListAttachments (limit 1..1000, offset non-negative). The read runs in one
779	// serialized transaction and writes nothing.
780	func (s *Store) ListAttachmentAccess(callerDeviceID, attachmentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]string, error) {
781		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
782		if err != nil {
783			return nil, err
784		}
785		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
786	
787		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID)
788		if err != nil {
789			return nil, err
790		}
791		if a.DeviceID != callerDeviceID {
792			return nil, ErrAttachmentForbidden
793		}
794	
795		rows, err := tx.Query(
796			`SELECT ac.device_id FROM attachment_access ac
797			 WHERE ac.attachment_id = ? AND ac.authorized <> 0 AND ac.device_id <> ?
798			 ORDER BY ac.granted_seq ASC, ac.device_id ASC
799			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
800			attachmentID, a.DeviceID, limit, offset,
801		)
802		if err != nil {
803			return nil, err
804		}
805		devices := make([]string, 0)
806		for rows.Next() {
807			var deviceID string
808			if err := rows.Scan(&deviceID); err != nil {
809				_ = rows.Close()
810				return nil, err
811			}
812			devices = append(devices, deviceID)
813		}
814		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
815			_ = rows.Close()
816			return nil, err
817		}
818		_ = rows.Close()
819	
820		return devices, tx.Commit()
821	}
822

824		if len(a) != len(b) {

826		}
827		for i := range a {

832		return true

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
33	// shared database connection.
34	type App struct {
35		*store.Store
36	
37		events *events.Service
38		crdt   *crdt.Service
39	
40		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
41		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
42		// it through their gates rather than this field.
43		Authz *authz.Service
44	}
45	
46	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
47	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
48	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
49	// leaves nothing behind.
50	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
51		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55	
56		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
57		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
58		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
59		if err != nil {
60			_ = kernel.Close()
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
64		if err != nil {
65			_ = kernel.Close()
66			return nil, err
67		}
68		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
69		if err != nil {
70			_ = kernel.Close()
71			return nil, err
72		}
73	
74		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
75		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
76		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
77		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
78		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
79	
80		return &App{
81			Store:  kernel,
82			events: eventService,
83			crdt:   crdtService,
84			Authz:  permissions,
85		}, nil
86	}
87	
88	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
89	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
90	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
91	
92	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
93		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
94	}
95	
96	// Events returns the change event service.
97	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
98	
99	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
100	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
101	
102	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
103	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
104	
105	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
106	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
107	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
108	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
109	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
110		a.events.InterruptWaits()
111		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
112	}
113	
114	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
115	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
116		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
117	}
118	
119	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
120	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
121	func (a *App) Close() error {
122		a.events.InterruptWaits()
123		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
124		a.events.WaitDrained()
125		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
126		return a.Store.Close()
127	}
128	
129	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
130	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
131		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
132	}
133	
134	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
135	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
136		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
137	}
138	
139	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
140	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
141		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)

190	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
191	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
192	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
193	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
194	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
195	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
196	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
197	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
198	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
199	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
200	//
201	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
202	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
203	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
204	// immediately, stickily.
205	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
206		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
207		if err != nil {
208			return err
209		}
210		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
211	
212		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
213			return err
214		}
215		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
219			return err
220		}
221	
222		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
223		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
224		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
225		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
226		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
227		return nil
228	}

82	// NewHandlerWithReadiness builds the same public HTTP surface as NewHandler but
83	// answers every request — including GET /healthz — with a 503 JSON error until
84	// ready reports that the database is open and the listener is accepting
85	// connections. Once ready, responses are byte-for-byte what NewHandler emits;
86	// readiness is one-way, so a later flip back is not part of the contract.
87	func NewHandlerWithReadiness(s *app.App, ready func() bool) http.Handler {
88		h := NewHandler(s)
89		if ready == nil {
90			return h
91		}

93			if !ready() {
94				writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is not ready")
95				return
96			}
97			h.ServeHTTP(w, r)
98		})
99	}

351		// /v1/documents//..., /v1/devices//sessions or
352		// /v1/sessions//documents/...) as an unclean path and answers with a 307
353		// HTML redirect (a 404 in a real client). The API contract is a 400 JSON
354		// error for an empty identifier, so intercept those paths before the mux
355		// sees them. A trailing slash empties the final id of the device/session
356		// routes and is rejected there for the same reason; the document routes
357		// keep their pre-existing ServeMux behavior.
358		return emptyIDGuard(mux)
359	}

361	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
362	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
363	// plain-text 404.
364	//
365	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
366	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
367	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
368	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
369	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
370	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
371		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
372			p := r.URL.Path
373	
374			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
375			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
376			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
377				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
378			}
379	
380			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) {
381				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
382				return
383			}
384			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
385		})
386	}

388	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
389	// long-poll/replay/compaction endpoints but is not that endpoint's exact
390	// location: a missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra segments, or a
391	// "poll"/"replay"/"compact" segment in a position short of the registered
392	// shape. ServeMux would answer those with a 301 redirect or a plain-text
393	// 404/405; the new endpoints promise a JSON error and never a redirect, so
394	// every such path is a malformed 400.
395	//
396	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
397	// happen to be named "poll", "replay" or "compact" keep their ordinary
398	// merge/snapshot/changes routes.
399	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
400		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
401		if !ok {
402			return false
403		}
404		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
405	
406		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
407		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
408		for i, seg := range segs {
409			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
410				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
411			}
412		}
413		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
414		// non-empty documentID.
415		for i, seg := range segs {
416			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
417				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
418			}
419		}
420		// Compaction endpoint: "compact" must be exactly the third segment, after
421		// a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace has its own
422		// guard; "compact" there is the CRDT compaction keyword, not the
423		// change-log one.
424		for i, seg := range segs {
425			if seg == "compact" && i > 0 {
426				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
427					return false
428				}
429				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
430			}
431		}
432		return false
433	}

435	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
436	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
437	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
438	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
439	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
440	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
441	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
442	//
443	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
444	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
445	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
446	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
447	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
448	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
449		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
450		if !ok {
451			return false
452		}
453		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
454		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
455		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
456		// keyword.
457		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
458			return false
459		}
460		for i, seg := range segs {
461			if seg != "subscribe" {
462				continue
463			}
464			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
465			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
466			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
467				continue
468			}
469			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
470			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
471			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
472			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
473				segs[0] != "" &&
474				segs[1] == "documents" &&
475				segs[2] != "" &&
476				segs[3] == "changes" {
477				return false
478			}
479			return true
480		}
481		return false
482	}

484	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
485	// namespace but is not at one of its two exact locations:
486	//
487	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
488	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
489	//
490	// a missing "state"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or a "crdt" segment
491	// in the keyword position (immediately past the document identifier) short of
492	// one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer those with a
493	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a JSON 400
494	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
495	//
496	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
497	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
498	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
499	// keeps its ordinary routes.
500	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
501		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
502		if !ok {
503			return false
504		}
505		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
506		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
507			return false
508		}
509		// Keyword position reached. The state read is exactly
510		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state; the subscription adds
511		// one trailing "subscribe" segment.
512		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
513			segs[0] != "" &&
514			segs[2] != "" &&
515			segs[4] == "state"
516		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
517			segs[0] != "" &&
518			segs[2] != "" &&
519			segs[4] == "state" &&
520			segs[5] == "subscribe"
521		return !(validState || validSubscribe)
522	}
